card.name: Words setting a level or limit
card.fires_on: Words that mark a threshold or range just before a number or reference amount, such as up to, lower than, levels as low as, or above. Seen in dose, exposure and severity-stage text.

modes.label: Up to / lower than
modes.description: Small linking words that introduce an upper limit or comparison to an exposure or dose.
modes.example: gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms were reported with daily doses up<< to>> 6,000 mg/day

modes.label: Level words
modes.description: The noun level(s) used for a concentration or stage of disease.
modes.example: symptoms of toxicity have been reported at<< levels>> as low as 800 ng

modes.label: Ascending or above
modes.description: Words about direction or rank along a scale, such as ascending or above.
modes.example: spinal cord injuries at T-6 or<< above>>, communication difficulties

card.plain: It fires on words that set a limit or point on a scale, like "up to" or "lower than", right before the amount.
